//: Typecheck project for the test suites — a known-red baseline, not yet wired into the gate.
//why: `tsconfig.base.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`, and `exclude` beats `include`, so every package's `tsc --noEmit` skips the suites: 380 test files were compiled by no gate at all. This project overrides `exclude` to enrol them. It is a separate project on purpose — the package configs drive the build (`composite`, `rootDir: ./src`, emit), so a test file there is a TS6059 error, not merely unwanted output.
//baseline: Baseline after #97c: 1830 errors (#97b 2007, #97a 2295, 2342 before any of them — each ratchet step accounting for the difference). Dominant classes: TS4111 (574, index-signature access under `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`), TS2532/TS18047/TS18048 (598, possibly-null under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`), TS6133/TS6196 (347, unused declarations — in a test these are often a discarded input), TS2307 (111, module not found — the file has never executed), TS2345 (192). Run `pnpm typecheck:tests` to reproduce; the script exists so the number is checkable, and CI does not run it while it is this far from green.
//paths: Mirrors the `resolve.alias` entries in vitest.config.ts. Without them the compiler could not resolve a single workspace import made from the root tests/** tree: 99 TS2307 errors, and every type behind those imports was invisible to the gate.
//module: The suites run under vitest/vite, whose resolver is a bundler's: the `paths` above already mirror `resolve.alias` for exactly that reason. `NodeNext` inherited from the base treated these files as CommonJS and rejected `import.meta`, which vite supports. Overriding here keeps the modelling honest — the test project describes how the tests actually run.
//paths-server: `graphql-e2e.test.ts` resolves these from the server's dependency tree at runtime via createRequire, because only that package declares them. These entries give the typecheck the same answer, as the entries above mirror vitest.config.ts.
